stem: A pure inductor is connected to an ac source. During the quarter cycle in which the magnitude of the current increases from zero to its maximum,
options: energy flows from the magnetic field of the inductor back to the source
energy is dissipated as heat in the windings of the inductor
energy flows from the source into the magnetic field of the inductor
no energy is exchanged between the source and the inductor coil
explanation: Correct option: (C). As |i| rises, the magnetic energy (1/2)Li² increases, so the source supplies energy that is stored in the magnetic field. In the next quarter cycle, when |i| falls, this energy returns to the source, which is why the average power is zero. A pure inductor has no resistance, so no heat is produced, and energy is certainly exchanged during each quarter.
